To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) WNT signaling is a barrier that restrains the progression of BRAF-induced lung cancer; and (2) inactivated WNT signaling is the trigger for oncogene-induced senescense (OIS).

WNT signaling and its downstream target, c-MYC, are required for early-stage proliferation of BRAFV(V600E)-driven lung tumors and are inactivated in the senescence state, and pharmacological inhibition of WNT signaling with the Porcupine inhibitor LGK974 suppresses the growth of early stage BRAFV(V(V600E)-dependent lung tumors.
